questions.question:
If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

51 + 8 − 8 ÷ 80 × 4 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

Given equation: 51 + 8 − 8 ÷ 80 × 4 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘-‘ and ‘×' and '÷’ are interchanged, then: 51 − 8 × 8 + 80 ÷ 4 = ?

⇒ 51 − 8 × 8 + (80 ÷ 4)

⇒ 51 − (8 × 8) + 20

⇒ 51 − 64 + 20

⇒ −13 + 20 = **7**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

⇒ (18 × 2) − (48 ÷ 4) + 21

⇒ 36 − 12 + 21

⇒ 24 + 21

⇒ 45

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All cars are buses.

Some cars are trucks.

Conclusions (I): Some trucks are cars.

Conclusions (II): Some buses are cars.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All cars are buses.

Some cars are trucks.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/018e302c23acc3ee5ca98e71214217fbb40d6555d6d5e2c56b8b44f38853a627.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d60c63dd01cca40d2a704d92a5be3aeb396c82daa5bbae3079985dde28808a38.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some trucks are cars.

If there is an intersection between set A (Cars) and set C (Trucks), then it is always true that Some C are A.

Therefore, conclusion (I) logically follows.

II. Some buses are cars.

The statement All A are B always implies that Some B are A. (Since all cars are buses, the set of buses must contain the set of cars, meaning some members of the 'Buses' set are also 'Cars').

Therefore, conclusion (II) logically follows.

So, Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘FOUR’ is coded as ‘5427’ and ‘RISE’ is coded as ‘6143’. What is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0270f2b5240d1e3915517248ac98d6d73ad611166857551401277421991a6c6e.png] 

The logic followed here is:

‘FOUR’ is coded as ‘5427’

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/939c5e7a64d3bdb1d60427f3d3784fe3c661e679c182a927c175a29533bca203.png] 

‘RISE’ is coded as ‘6143’

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5476e14b9215ff9e68ea5aeb4016fd56d9e5a3bade6d2aeaf428aff10e7ea57.png] 

R is common in both words and 4 is common in both number codes.

So, '**4**' is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
